*** * *
 JUDGMENT The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That, on 21.3.2022 at about 11.00 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding in his Honda Splendor bearing registration No.KA-07-R-1696 near ITC factory, on Malur-Hosakote road, Malur Taluk, Kolar District, at that time, driver of car bearing registration No.KA-04- MG-7603 came from same direction in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and dashed against the motor cycle from behind.
As a result of which, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Bharani Hospital, Malur, then he was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical hospital, Kolar,
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medicines,
attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4.

sentences.text: It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 24 years, labourer and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month and he used to spend the said amount for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to accidental injuries.
5. It is contended that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-04-MG-7603.
In this regard, case was registered against driver of said vehicle by the jurisdictional Malur Police in Crime No.149/2022.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking compensation.
6. After registration of the case, notices were issued to the respondents.

In response to the notices,
the respondents have appeared through their respective counsel, inspite of sufficient opportunities given to the respondent No.1 has not filed his written statement.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has filed its written statement.

sentences.text: In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has admitted about the issuance of policy in respect of car bearing registration No.KA-04-MG-7603 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that the complaint was lodged on 23.3.2023,
there is delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner.
It is contended that, petitioner was riding the motor cycle without wearing headgear.

It is also contention of the respondent that the driver of offending vehicle does not posses valid D.L. on the date of accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Ultimately contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.

With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.
8.

On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident which was taken place on 21.3.2022 at about 11.00 a.m. opp.ITC factory on Malur-Hosakote road, Malur Taluk, Kolar District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Maruthi Alto car bearing No.KA-04-MG- 7603 in an actionable negligence?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What order or award?

9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, petitioner has placed his affidavit evidence in lieu of examination-in-chief, who examined as PW1 and got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.
10.
On the other hand, the respondents have not adduced either oral or documentary evidence on their behalf.

11. Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.
12.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3:

As per final order,

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-04-MG-7603 the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, but strogly disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle though appeared through his counsel but failed to file his written statement.

15. In the light of the rival contentions of both the parties, on going through the above issue burden is on the petitioner to prove the above issue on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
16. The petitioner in order to prove his case got examined himself as PW1.
He has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon police documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P6.
Ex.P1-copy of F.I.R. Ex.P2-copy of the first information statement,
Ex.P3- copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P4-copy of IMV report, Ex.P5- copy of wound certificate and Ex.P6-copy of charge sheet.

17. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Malur Police station has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279 & 337 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the Investigation Officer of the case has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
18.

Though the respondent No.2 has disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, but not examined either the driver of the offending vehicle or any of the independent eye witness to prove its contention.
19. Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defences of the respondent No.2 about the denial of allegation made against him.

20. In the light of the evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-04-MG-7603.
As such, the petitioner has placed satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, I am answering the issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
21.

The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

sentences.text:
Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injuries cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P5.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Contusion over left side forehead 2) Right foot II metatarsal fracture 3) Multiple abrasions all over body 24.
In connection with the above said injuries, the doctor is of the opinion that, the said injuries are grievous in nature.

The petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P7 issued by Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, which discloses that the petitioner was admitted from 21.3.2022 and discharged on 24.3.2022.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to speak about the grievousness of the injuries.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
25.
PW1 has stated that, he was working as a labourer at ITC Company, Industrial Area, Malur and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

There is no iota of documents to show that the petitioner was Chethan K M vs Sachin Yadav K N on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122653351/
5 earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

sentences.text: In the absence of the documents, it is apt to be considered notional income.
On perusal of discharge summary reveals that the petitioner was admitted from 21.3.2022 and discharged on 24.3.2022.
By considering the nature of the injuries definitely, there was some difficulty to him to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of one month.
by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.15,500/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
26.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence, placed medical bills of Rs.42,044/- as per Ex.P11 along with prescriptions at Ex.P10.
There are no contra materials available on record to disprove the medical bills.
On perusal of the medical bills Sl.No.10 Rs.400/-, Sl.No.11 Rs.200/- & Sl.No.12 Rs.100/- is not having any seal and signature.
The said amount shall not be considered.
After deducting the said amount, it comes to Rs.41,344/-.

Hence,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.41,344/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
27.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food,
nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
28.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.

Except production of medical documents and averments made in the main petition as well as in the chief affidavit, has not made an effort to examine the treated doctor,
in order to prove the disability sustained by him, due to the accidental injuries in order to know,
whether the injuries sustained by the petitioner will effect to his future and whether the said injuries will make any discomfort to the petitioner to do his routine work as well as his work for his avocation.
In such a situation, court cannot consider the loss of future income, in the absence of convincing evidence from the side of the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for the compensation under the head of loss of future income due to want of evidence on record.

Loss of amenities;
29.

PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries, petitioner cannot walk, sit,
squat, climb the stairs.

On perusal of evidence of PW1 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood as a mason.

Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.3,000/-
towards loss of amenities.

The claim petition filed by the petitioner u/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.
